sections.title: Down to your device, up to the internet
sections.content: You know *le-* (down) and *fel-* (up) from A1 and from Unit 22. On a computer they give the two verbs you need: *letölt* ("to download"; *le-* + *tölt*, "to fill") and *feltölt* ("to upload"). Both take an object, so you choose between the endings you know from A1: *Letöltök egy fájlt.* for a file in general (indefinite) and *Letöltöm a fájlt.* for the file (definite). Plurals work as usual: *Feltöltöm a képeket.* ("I upload the pictures.")

items.english: I download a file from the e-mail.
I upload the pictures to the website.

items.spanish: Letöltöm a fájlt, aztán küldöm Katának.
items.english: I download the file, then I send it to Kata.

sections.content: Mixing up the direction is the usual slip. You load something up to the internet (*feltölt*) and down to your own device (*letölt*), just as *felmegy* goes up and *lemegy* goes down.
